column1: Where does Azure Cloud Shell mount its persistent file share inside the backing Linux container?
column2: At the directory `/home/<user>/clouddrive`.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Storage Mount
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 3; MS Learn Cloud Shell Overview

column1: Which Azure storage service provides the persistent storage volume for Azure Cloud Shell?
column2: Azure Files (an Azure File Share).
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Backing Storage Service
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 3; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 3

column1: How long can an Azure Cloud Shell session remain idle before it automatically times out and disconnects?
column2: 20 minutes of inactivity.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Inactivity Timeout
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 3; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 4

column1: What happens to files stored outside of `/home/<user>/clouddrive` (such as in `/tmp`) when a Cloud Shell session terminates?
column2: They are permanently discarded because the temporary container host is deallocated.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Storage Persistence Scope
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 3

column1: Do Bash and PowerShell environments in Azure Cloud Shell share the same persistent storage file share?
column2: Yes, both Bash and PowerShell attach to the exact same `clouddrive` Azure Files share.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Shell Environment Parity
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 4

column1: Which CLI command opens the integrated Monaco-based text editor in Azure Cloud Shell Classic mode?
column2: The `code` command (e.g., `code <filename>`).
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Built-in Text Editor
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 3; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 5

column1: Can an administrator execute `sudo` commands or gain root privileges inside the Azure Cloud Shell container?
column2: No, Cloud Shell provides a standard unprivileged user container without `sudo` access.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Administrator Permissions
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 4

column1: What direct URL allows accessing Azure Cloud Shell full-screen in a standalone browser window?
column2: `https://shell.azure.com`
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Direct Web Access
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 3

column1: How is the backing infrastructure of Azure Cloud Shell secured against data-at-rest threats by default?
column2: It is compliant with double encryption at rest by default without requiring user configuration.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Encryption at Rest
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 2

column1: How many concurrent active Cloud Shell instances can a single user run simultaneously?
column2: Only one instance at a time per user account.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Concurrent Session Limit
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 4

column1: When setting up Cloud Shell with Advanced Settings, which three existing resource components can you explicitly specify?
column2: An existing Resource Group, Storage Account, and File Share.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Advanced Storage Configuration
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 3

column1: Can a single Azure Cloud Shell storage account be spread across multiple Azure regions simultaneously?
column2: No, the allocated storage account is pinned to a single designated Azure region.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Regional Affinity
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 4

column1: On which operating system kernel do both the Bash and PowerShell Cloud Shell containers execute?
column2: A Linux container environment (CBL-Mariner / Ubuntu).
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Host Operating System
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 4

column1: Who is responsible for updating the Azure CLI (`az`) and Azure PowerShell (`Az`) modules in Cloud Shell?
column2: Microsoft automatically maintains and updates all modules in the hosted container.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Module Updates
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 2

column1: Name two third-party Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools preinstalled in Azure Cloud Shell.
column2: Terraform and Ansible.
column3: Azure Cloud Shell - Built-in IaC Tools
column4: MS Learn Intro to Cloud Shell, Unit 3 table

column1: What syntax style do ARM templates use to define resources compared to imperative scripts?
column2: Declarative syntax (defining what the target state looks like rather than step-by-step commands).
column3: ARM Templates - Syntax Type
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 2; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 131

column1: What does it mean that ARM template deployments are 'idempotent'?
column2: Deploying the same template repeatedly results in the exact same resource state without unintended duplicate side effects.
column3: ARM Templates - Idempotency
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 2; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 131

column1: What happens to existing resources not defined in the template when deploying in Incremental Mode?
column2: Existing resources are left untouched and unchanged.
column3: ARM Templates - Incremental vs Complete Mode
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 132; MS Learn ARM Deployment Modes

column1: What happens to existing resources in the resource group that are NOT defined in the template when deploying in Complete Mode?
column2: Resource Manager permanently deletes them (unless prevented by locks or specific resource behaviors).
column3: ARM Templates - Complete Mode Deletion
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 132

column1: What is the default deployment mode when deploying an ARM template via CLI or PowerShell if not specified?
column2: Incremental Mode.
column3: ARM Templates - Default Deployment Mode
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 132

column1: Name the four primary top-level sections in an ARM template used to define inputs, values, infrastructure, and return data.
column2: `parameters`, `variables`, `resources`, and `outputs`.
column3: ARM Templates - JSON Top-Level Sections
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 2; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 131

column1: What is the purpose of the `parameters` section in an ARM template?
column2: To allow external values to be passed in at deployment time, making the template reusable across environments.
column3: ARM Templates - Parameters Purpose
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 4

column1: How do `variables` differ from `parameters` in an ARM template?
column2: `variables` are calculated internally within the template and cannot be overridden by external deployment inputs.
column3: ARM Templates - Variables Purpose
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 4; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 131

column1: What does the ARM template function `uniqueString()` return, and why is it used?
column2: A 13-character deterministic hash based on input strings, commonly used to create globally unique resource names.
column3: ARM Templates - uniqueString Function
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 4; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 133

column1: What expression should you use in an ARM template to set a resource location to match its containing resource group?
column2: `[resourceGroup().location]`
column3: ARM Templates - Dynamic Location Best Practice
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 4; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 133

column1: Which ARM template property explicitly enforces the sequential deployment order of dependent resources?
column2: The `dependsOn` property array.
column3: ARM Templates - Resource Dependencies
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 2; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 134

column1: How does Azure Resource Manager handle the deployment of multiple independent resources defined in a template?
column2: It deploys them in parallel to maximize deployment speed.
column3: ARM Templates - Parallel Execution
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 2

column1: Which ARM deployment feature allows administrators to preview resource changes and deletions before applying a template?
column2: The What-If operation (`az deployment group what-if` or `Get-AzResourceGroupDeploymentWhatIfResult`).
column3: ARM Templates - What-If Operation
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 133

column1: How can you validate an ARM template syntax and quota checks without actually provisioning resources?
column2: Using `az deployment group validate` or `Test-AzResourceGroupDeployment`.
column3: ARM Templates - Pre-Deployment Validation
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 3; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 133

column1: What is the primary function of the `outputs` section in an ARM template?
column2: To return values generated during deployment (such as provisioned IP addresses or FQDNs) back to the caller.
column3: ARM Templates - Outputs Section
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 4; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 131

column1: Name two parameter constraint attributes you can define in an ARM template to restrict valid inputs.
column2: `allowedValues` and `minValue`/`maxValue` (or `minLength`/`maxLength`).
column3: ARM Templates - Parameter Constraints
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 4

column1: How are external parameter values conventionally provided to an ARM template deployment?
column2: Through a JSON parameter file (e.g., `azuredeploy.parameters.json`).
column3: ARM Templates - Parameter File Extension
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 132

column1: What is the relationship between Azure Bicep code and ARM JSON templates?
column2: Bicep is a domain-specific language that compiles directly down to standard ARM JSON templates.
column3: ARM Templates - Bicep Relationship
column4: MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 1 note; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 135

column1: What primary syntax advantages does Azure Bicep offer compared to JSON ARM templates?
column2: Bicep provides cleaner concise syntax, direct module reuse, automatic dependency management via symbolic names, and eliminates complex JSON bracket escaping.
column3: Bicep - Syntax Advantages
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 135; MS Learn Bicep Basics, Unit 2

column1: What CLI command converts an existing ARM JSON template into an equivalent Bicep file?
column2: `az bicep decompile --file <template.json>`
column3: Bicep - Decompiling ARM JSON
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 137; MS Learn Bicep Basics, Unit 5

column1: Where can you export an existing resource group's configuration as an ARM template?
column2: In the Azure Portal under Resource Group > 'Export template', or under Resource Group > 'Deployments' history.
column3: ARM Templates - Export Deployment
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 134; MS Learn Deploy Infrastructure ARM, Unit 5

column1: Which Azure CLI command directly deploys a `.bicep` file to a resource group without precompiling to JSON?
column2: `az deployment group create --resource-group <rg> --template-file <main.bicep>`
column3: Bicep - Direct Deployment Command
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 3, p. 136; MS Learn Bicep Basics, Unit 3

column1: Which modern authentication protocols does Microsoft Entra ID support natively for web and cloud applications?
column2: SAML 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), OAuth 2.0, and WS-Federation.
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Authentication Protocols
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 2; MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 2

column1: Does Microsoft Entra ID natively support legacy Kerberos and NTLM authentication without add-on domain services?
column2: No, native Entra ID uses HTTP-based web protocols; Kerberos and NTLM require Active Directory Domain Services or Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Protocol Differences vs AD DS
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 3; MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 2

column1: What minimum Microsoft Entra ID edition is required for dynamic group membership and on-premises password writeback?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID P1.
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Edition Requirements for P1
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 4; MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 4

column1: Which advanced security features specifically require Microsoft Entra ID P2 licenses?
column2: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) and Microsoft Entra ID Protection (risk-based Conditional Access).
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Edition Requirements for P2
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 4; MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 4

column1: What domain suffix is assigned by default to a newly created Microsoft Entra ID tenant before adding a custom domain?
column2: `.onmicrosoft.com` (e.g., `contoso.onmicrosoft.com`).
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Default Domain Name
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 7; MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 3

column1: Which DNS record type is typically created at your domain registrar to verify domain ownership in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: A DNS TXT record (or alternately an MX record).
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Custom Domain Verification Record
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 7; MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 3

column1: What is a Microsoft Entra ID tenant?
column2: A dedicated, isolated instance of Microsoft Entra ID that represents an organization and houses its directory objects.
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Tenant Definition
column4: MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 2

column1: Can you delete the initial `.onmicrosoft.com` domain name from a Microsoft Entra ID tenant?
column2: No, the initial `.onmicrosoft.com` domain is immutable and cannot be deleted or renamed.
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Primary Domain Name Deletion
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 8

column1: Can an Azure subscription trust more than one Microsoft Entra ID tenant simultaneously?
column2: No, each Azure subscription can trust only one Microsoft Entra tenant at a time.
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Subscription Directory Association
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 11; MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 3

column1: Can multiple Azure subscriptions trust the same Microsoft Entra ID tenant?
column2: Yes, a single tenant can be trusted by multiple subscriptions.
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Single Tenant Multiple Subscriptions
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 11

column1: Does Microsoft Entra ID use Organizational Units (OUs) and Group Policy Objects (GPOs) like Windows Server AD?
column2: No, Entra ID is a flat directory structure without OUs or native Active Directory GPOs.
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Flat vs Hierarchical Structure
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 3

column1: Which tool synchronizes on-premises Active Directory objects into Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Microsoft Entra Connect (or Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync).
column3: Microsoft Entra ID - Hybrid Identity Sync Tool
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 5; MS Learn Understand Entra ID, Unit 4

column1: What are the three primary types of user accounts in Microsoft Entra ID based on their origin?
column2: Cloud identities (created natively in Entra ID), Directory-synced identities (synced from on-premises AD), and Guest identities (B2B invited users).
column3: Identity Management - User Types
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 13; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 2

column1: How long does a deleted user remain in the 'Deleted users' recycle bin before permanent deletion?
column2: 30 days (during which it can be restored with its original permissions intact).
column3: Identity Management - Deleted User Soft-Delete Window
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 15; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 3

column1: What file format is required when performing bulk user creation or group membership updates in Microsoft Entra admin center?
column2: CSV (Comma-Separated Values) format using Microsoft's downloadable template.
column3: Identity Management - Bulk Operations Format
column4: MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 4; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 17

column1: What are the two types of groups supported in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Security groups and Microsoft 365 groups.
column3: Identity Management - Group Types
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 19; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 6

column1: Which group type in Entra ID is best suited for assigning RBAC roles and resource permissions?
column2: Security groups.
column3: Identity Management - Security Groups vs M365 Groups
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 19; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 6

column1: What are the three membership types available for Microsoft Entra ID groups?
column2: Assigned (manual), Dynamic User, and Dynamic Device.
column3: Identity Management - Group Membership Types
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 20; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 6

column1: How are members added to or removed from a Dynamic User group in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Automatically evaluated by rules based on user object attributes (e.g., `(user.department -eq "Sales")`).
column3: Identity Management - Dynamic Group Query Evaluation
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 21; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 7

column1: What is the benefit of group-based licensing in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Licenses (such as M365 or Entra P1) are automatically assigned or revoked as users join or leave the group.
column3: Identity Management - Group-Based Licensing
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 23; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 8

column1: Does Azure RBAC support role assignments to nested groups?
column2: No, Azure role assignments only apply to direct group members; nested group members are not granted access.
column3: Identity Management - Group Nesting Limitation in RBAC
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 20

column1: When an external partner user is invited via Entra B2B Collaboration, where does their primary authentication take place?
column2: In their home identity provider (e.g., their organization's Entra ID, Google, or Microsoft account).
column3: Identity Management - B2B Collaboration Guest Redirection
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 14; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 5

column1: What two components compose a User Principal Name (UPN) in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: The username prefix and the domain suffix, separated by an `@` symbol (e.g., `user@domain.com`).
column3: Identity Management - User Principal Name (UPN) Structure
column4: MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 2

column1: What Entra ID resource allows delegating administrative control over a specific subset of users and groups without granting tenant-wide admin rights?
column2: Administrative Units (AUs).
column3: Identity Management - Administrative Units (AUs)
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 25; MS Learn Manage Identities, Unit 9

column1: What is the maximum supported hierarchy depth for Management Groups in Azure?
column2: Up to 6 levels of depth (excluding the Root Management Group).
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Management Groups Hierarchy Depth
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 29; MS Learn Architectural Components, Unit 4

column1: What is the name of the top-level container automatically created in every tenant to govern all management groups and subscriptions?
column2: Tenant Root Group.
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Root Management Group Name
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 30; MS Learn Architectural Components, Unit 4

column1: How many total Management Groups can be created within a single Microsoft Entra tenant?
column2: Up to 10,000 Management Groups.
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Management Groups Directory Limit
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 30; MS Learn Architectural Components, Unit 4

column1: Can a Management Group or subscription have more than one parent Management Group?
column2: No, each Management Group or subscription can have exactly one parent.
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Management Group Parent Assignment
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 30

column1: What are the four levels of management scope in Azure from broadest to most specific?
column2: Management Group -> Subscription -> Resource Group -> Resource.
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Four Levels of Scope
column4: MS Learn Architectural Components, Unit 2; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 28

column1: Can an individual Azure resource belong to more than one Resource Group at the same time?
column2: No, an Azure resource can only exist in exactly one Resource Group.
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Resource Group Membership Rule
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 35; MS Learn Architectural Components, Unit 5

column1: Can a Resource Group contain resources located in different geographic regions than the Resource Group itself?
column2: Yes, resources inside a Resource Group can be located in any supported Azure region.
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Resource Group Regional Distribution
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 35; MS Learn Architectural Components, Unit 5

column1: What happens to the resources inside a Resource Group when the Resource Group is deleted?
column2: All resources inside the Resource Group are permanently deleted.
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Resource Group Deletion Cascade
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 36

column1: Can resources be moved from one Resource Group to another or to another subscription?
column2: Yes, supported resources can be moved between Resource Groups and between subscriptions without downtime.
column3: Azure Hierarchy - Moving Resources Across Resource Groups
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 37

column1: What are the two types of resource locks supported in Azure Resource Manager?
column2: `CanNotDelete` (Delete lock) and `ReadOnly` (Read-only lock).
column3: Resource Locks - Lock Types
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 39; MS Learn Architectural Components, Unit 6

column1: What operations are allowed on a resource protected by a `CanNotDelete` lock?
column2: Authorized users can read and modify the resource, but cannot delete it.
column3: Resource Locks - CanNotDelete Behavior
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 39

column1: Why does a `ReadOnly` lock on a storage account prevent users from listing account access keys?
column2: Because listing keys is a POST request that returns write-capable credentials, which the `ReadOnly` lock blocks.
column3: Resource Locks - ReadOnly Side Effects on Storage
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 40

column1: What is the primary function of Azure Policy compared to Azure RBAC?
column2: Azure Policy governs resource properties, configurations, and compliance, whereas RBAC controls user actions and permissions.
column3: Azure Policy - Core Purpose
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 42; MS Learn Azure Policy, Unit 2

column1: What is an Azure Policy Initiative (also called a Policy Set)?
column2: A collection of multiple policy definitions grouped together toward a single overarching compliance goal.
column3: Azure Policy - Definition vs Initiative
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 44; MS Learn Azure Policy, Unit 3

column1: What happens when a resource deployment fails compliance with an Azure Policy having the `Deny` effect?
column2: The Resource Manager request is immediately rejected and the deployment fails.
column3: Azure Policy - Deny Effect
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 43; MS Learn Azure Policy, Unit 4

column1: Does an Azure Policy with the `Audit` effect block a non-compliant resource from being created?
column2: No, the resource is created, but a non-compliance warning is logged in the compliance dashboard.
column3: Azure Policy - Audit Effect
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 43

column1: Which Azure Policy effect adds defined fields or tags to a resource during creation or update?
column2: The `Append` effect (or `Modify` effect).
column3: Azure Policy - Append vs Modify Effect
column4: MS Learn Azure Policy, Unit 4; Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 43

column1: What does an Azure Policy with the `DeployIfNotExists` effect do when a condition is met?
column2: It automatically deploys a related resource or extension (such as a Log Analytics agent) if it is missing.
column3: Azure Policy - DeployIfNotExists Effect
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 44; MS Learn Azure Policy, Unit 4

column1: How are existing non-compliant resources brought into compliance for `Modify` or `DeployIfNotExists` policies?
column2: By creating an Azure Policy Remediation Task, which uses a managed identity to remediate existing resources.
column3: Azure Policy - Remediation Tasks
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 47; MS Learn Azure Policy, Unit 5

column1: When does Azure Policy automatically evaluate compliance on resources?
column2: During resource creation/update (PUT/PATCH), when a policy is assigned, and periodically every 24 hours.
column3: Azure Policy - Evaluation Triggers
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 45

column1: Can an administrator exclude specific resource groups or resources from an assigned policy at a higher scope?
column2: Yes, by adding specific scopes to the 'Exclusions' list of the policy assignment.
column3: Azure Policy - Exclusions Scope
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 46; MS Learn Azure Policy, Unit 3

column1: If an Azure Policy is assigned at a Management Group, where is that policy enforced?
column2: Across all subscriptions, resource groups, and resources residing under that Management Group.
column3: Azure Policy - Scope Inheritance
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 45

column1: What JSON block inside an Azure Policy definition contains the `if`/`then` conditional rules?
column2: The `policyRule` block.
column3: Azure Policy - Definition Structure
column4: MS Learn Azure Policy, Unit 4

column1: What is the purpose of setting a policy effect to `Disabled`?
column2: It stops the policy rule from evaluating or enforcing compliance without having to delete the assignment.
column3: Azure Policy - Disabled Effect
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 44

column1: What three elements are required to construct an Azure RBAC role assignment?
column2: A Security Principal (who), a Role Definition (what permissions), and a Scope (where).
column3: Azure RBAC - Three Elements of Role Assignment
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 48; MS Learn Secure Resources with RBAC, Unit 2

column1: What distinct permission differentiates the `Owner` role from the `Contributor` role in Azure RBAC?
column2: The `Owner` role can grant and manage access permissions (RBAC) to others, whereas `Contributor` cannot.
column3: Azure RBAC - Owner Role Permissions
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 49; MS Learn Secure Resources with RBAC, Unit 3

column1: Can a user assigned the built-in `Contributor` role assign RBAC permissions to another user?
column2: No, `Contributor` has `Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write` excluded.
column3: Azure RBAC - Contributor Role Permissions
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 49

column1: Can a user with the `Reader` role view the access keys of an Azure Storage account?
column2: No, viewing access keys is a management plane action that requires `listKeys` write permissions.
column3: Azure RBAC - Reader Role Permissions
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 50

column1: What is the primary function of the built-in `User Access Administrator` role?
column2: To manage user access and role assignments without granting management access to the resources themselves.
column3: Azure RBAC - User Access Administrator Role
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 50; MS Learn Secure Resources with RBAC, Unit 3

column1: Which properties in a custom role JSON definition define granted permissions, excluded permissions, and valid deployment targets?
column2: `Actions`, `NotActions`, and `AssignableScopes`.
column3: Azure RBAC - Custom Role Definition Sections
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 52; MS Learn Secure Resources with RBAC, Unit 4

column1: Does listing an operation in `NotActions` act as a deny rule if the user is granted that permission via another role?
column2: No, `NotActions` simply subtracts permissions from `Actions`; it does NOT override permissions granted by another role.
column3: Azure RBAC - NotActions Behavior
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 53

column1: How do Azure Deny Assignments interact with RBAC allow permissions?
column2: Deny assignments take absolute precedence over allow role assignments.
column3: Azure RBAC - Deny Assignments Priority
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 54; MS Learn Secure Resources with RBAC, Unit 2

column1: What is the difference between `Actions` and `DataActions` in an RBAC role definition?
column2: `Actions` apply to the control/management plane (e.g., creating a VM), while `DataActions` apply to data plane operations (e.g., reading blobs).
column3: Azure RBAC - DataActions vs Actions
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 53

column1: If a user is assigned `Contributor` at the Subscription level, what role permissions do they have on a Resource Group in that subscription?
column2: They inherit full `Contributor` permissions on the Resource Group and all resources inside it.
column3: Azure RBAC - Scope Inheritance Rule
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 48

column1: At which scopes can an Azure custom RBAC role be defined in `AssignableScopes`?
column2: At Management Groups, Subscriptions, or Resource Groups (cannot specify individual resources).
column3: Azure RBAC - Custom Roles AssignableScopes Limit
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 54

column1: How can a Global Administrator in Entra ID gain access to manage all Azure subscriptions in their tenant?
column2: By turning on the 'Access management for Azure resources' switch, which grants `User Access Administrator` at the Root Management Group.
column3: Azure RBAC - Elevated Access Global Admin
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 51

column1: Can Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) be enabled for a select group of pilot users in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Yes, SSPR scope options are 'None', 'Selected' (specific group), or 'All'.
column3: Entra SSPR - Target Group Scope
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 1, p. 56; MS Learn SSPR, Unit 3

column1: What is the purpose of Microsoft Entra SSPR Password Writeback?

column2: A point-in-time snapshot of the disks taken when the VM was shut down, or if the VSS/snapshot extension failed during execution.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Crash-Consistent Backup
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 341; MS Learn Protect VMs with Backup, Unit 3

column1: What is the configurable retention range for the Instant Restore snapshot tier in an Azure VM backup policy?
column2: Between 1 and 5 days (default is 2 days).
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Instant Restore Duration
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 342; MS Learn Protect VMs with Backup, Unit 4

column1: Name the four restore options available when restoring an Azure Virtual Machine backup.
column2: Create New VM, Restore Disks, Replace Existing VM Disks, and Item-Level Recovery (ILR).
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Restore Options Available
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 344; MS Learn Protect VMs with Backup, Unit 5

column1: How does Item Level Recovery (ILR) allow you to recover specific individual files from an Azure VM backup?
column2: It generates an executable script that mounts recovery point disks as local iSCSI volumes on any machine for 12 hours.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Item Level Recovery (ILR) Mechanism
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 345; MS Learn Protect VMs with Backup, Unit 5

column1: What are the two phases of an Azure VM backup job?
column2: Phase 1: Taking a local disk snapshot (Instant Restore); Phase 2: Transferring the snapshot data to the Recovery Services Vault.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Two Phases of VM Backup
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 340; MS Learn Protect VMs with Backup, Unit 2

column1: What is the operational advantage of the 'Replace Existing' restore option for an Azure VM?
column2: It swaps the VM's corrupted OS and data disks with the backup disks without changing the VM resource ID, MAC, or IP address.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Replace Existing Disk Benefit
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 344

column1: What four retention tiers are available in Grandfather-Father-Son (GFS) backup policies in Azure?
column2: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Yearly retention points.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - GFS Retention Schema
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 343; MS Learn Protect VMs with Backup, Unit 4

column1: Is an agent required inside an Azure Virtual Machine to perform Azure VM backup?
column2: No, the Azure platform automatically injects the required snapshot extension into the Azure VM agent.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Backup Agent in Guest
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 340

column1: Can you exclude specific data disks (such as temporary scratch disks) from an Azure VM backup policy?
column2: Yes, selective disk backup allows including only the OS disk or specific data disks.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Selective Disk Backup
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 342

column1: What outbound network connectivity does an Azure VM require for backup extension communication?
column2: HTTPS connectivity to Azure public IP ranges (Azure Backup service tags and Azure Storage).
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Outbound Network Requirement for Backup
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 340; MS Learn Protect VMs with Backup, Unit 2

column1: What purpose do pre-script and post-script files serve during Linux Azure VM backups?
column2: They quiesce application I/O and flush cache to disk before snapshotting to ensure Application-Consistent backups on Linux.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Linux Pre/Post Scripts Purpose
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 341

column1: When restoring disks from a backup, what resource must you designate to receive the restored VHD files?
column2: A staging Storage Account (or target Resource Group for managed disks).
column3: Protect Azure VMs - Managed Disks Staging Storage
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 344

column1: Can Azure VMs encrypted with Azure Disk Encryption (ADE) be restored using Item-Level Recovery (ILR)?
column2: No, ILR does not support ADE-encrypted VMs; you must restore the full disk or VM.
column3: Protect Azure VMs - ADE Encrypted VM Restore
column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 345

column1: What are the two foundational data types collected by Azure Monitor?
column2: Metrics (numerical time-series values) and Logs (structured textual and record event data).

column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 310; MS Learn Monitor Azure VMs, Unit 2

column1: How long are standard Azure platform metrics retained in Azure Monitor without additional configuration?
column2: 93 days.

column1: Which query language is used to analyze log data stored in an Azure Log Analytics workspace?

column1: Why are Metric Alerts described as 'stateful' in Azure Monitor?

column1: What is an Action Group in Azure Monitor?

column4: Exam Ref AZ-104, Ch. 5, p. 316; MS Learn Monitor Azure VMs, Unit 4

column1: Which unified agent replaces the legacy Log Analytics agent (MMA/OMS) and Diagnostics extension on Azure VMs?

column1: What capabilities does VM Insights provide beyond basic VM monitoring?

column1: What is the configurable retention range for logs stored in an Azure Log Analytics Workspace?

column2: Application Performance Management (APM) monitoring code exceptions, request rates, response times, and live telemetry for web applications.
